prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one premium high-fidelity mobile website UI mockup for "hieu’s reviews", a private food journal for five real friends named Hieu, Ky-An, Vinh, Nick and Mai-Han. Portrait 1024x1536 pixels, website screenshot filling the image edge to edge, no phone hardware, browser chrome, perspective, outside captions or presentation frame. This is a new visual direction called THE SHARED NOTEBOOK: warm, clean, intimate, thoughtful, casually fun, designed to help friends log and rate a meal quickly. It should look like a real well-crafted app people want to use, not a marketing poster.

Design language: warm off-white #F8F6F0 page, forest-green #3F5846 ink and main button, soft pale celery #D9E6C6 only for the reviewer area and selected controls. A distinctive friendly humanist sans carries all UI text, medium-bold headings and loose whitespace. The notebook idea enters through a quiet left-aligned editorial layout and a few horizontal rules in the history, never fake paper, grain, spirals, ruled background, torn edges, skewed cards or photorealistic stationery. One small friendly outlined bowl mark in the header. Flat clean fills. Avoid dashboards, graphs, counters, floating metric cards, large illustrations and food photographs.

Precisely designed mobile composition:
- Header occupies roughly 7% height: tiny bowl icon and "hieu’s reviews" at left, quiet "Our places ↗" at right, a fine horizontal green divider.
- Main heading, clearly left aligned and compact: "Good food. Better company." in a friendly 32px-equivalent bold sans, on two lines. Under it, a short line "A little journal for our big opinions." This has warmth without stealing space from the task.
- Reviewer strip on a pale celery-green full-width simple band, NOT a nested card: "Who’s reviewing?" label followed by five circular pastel initial avatars, names beneath "Hieu", "Ky-An", "Vinh", "Nick", "Mai-Han". Hieu is visibly active with dark green ring and a small check badge. Actual generous touch targets; preserve full friend names.
- Below the strip, a white-ground, borderless compact review composer integrated into the page with a fine rule above. Heading "Log a meal". Input label "Where did you eat?" and a large empty search input with placeholder "Search our places or add one" and search icon. Then "How was it?" with a row of ten numbered buttons 1 through 10, selected 8 on dark green. Under that small line "8 / 10 · Worth another visit". Optional short one-line textarea labelled "Your take" with placeholder "What should the group know?". A quiet disclosure line "Add dishes, date or spending". Dark green full-width button "Save review" with small arrow. Keep main save within the first phone screen, with enough vertical breathing room and no redundant instructional blocks.
- Under a generous separator, section "Fresh from the group" with "See all" text link. Two compact journal entries as plain rows, no surrounding cards: a small coral H avatar, "Hieu at Little Dumpling", score "9.0 / 10", short note "Get the crispy-bottom dumplings."; then a pale blue N avatar, "Nick at Noodle House", "8.5 / 10", note "Spicy noodles. Zero regrets." Type real, legible, carefully aligned, names bold. A tiny label "Illustrative reviews".
- Bottom navigation with a flat off-white background and thin upper divider: outline journal icon "Journal", plus icon "Add review" in the selected green, location icon "Pick a place". No floating button over the content.

Make this structurally and typographically different from a restaurant receipt: OPEN layout, calm white space, celery friend strip, no enclosed ticket, no serif headline. The focal point is the short working review composer with visible friend choice. Perfect spelling, practical UI touch targets, excellent contrast, premium mobile product design.
